# Plan: SPE Round 1 for the Triage Agent

Your spec is one sentence: "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." This round turns that sentence into numbers. The agent is built, my predictions are recorded before any trial runs, and then one Workflow run grades the agent. The repo has no `spe/` folder yet, so this round creates it. I will make a local commit after each step. I will not push.

## Gaps in the spec

The spec does not define "correctly" or "cheaply." It also does not name the ticket fields or the label set. I have filled each gap with a default decision (D1 to D5). Approving this plan approves those defaults. You can change any of them before you approve.

| ID | Decision | Default |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Triage output | JSON with `category`, `priority`, `team`, `needs_human`, and `confidence` |
| D2 | Label set | Categories: billing, bug, account_access, feature_request, how_to, spam. Priorities: P1 to P4. Teams: Billing, Engineering, Support, Product. |
| D3 | "Correctly" | Category accuracy of at least 90%. P1 recall of at least 95%. Schema-valid output of at least 99%. |
| D4 | "Cheaply" | A mean cost of no more than $0.004 per ticket |
| D5 | Test data | 200 synthetic tickets, because you have not provided real tickets. A real-ticket sample replaces this set in round 2 if you can supply one. |

## 1. Specify

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Assign one category from the D2 set | User: "triage tickets correctly". D2. | `category_exact` |
| R2 | Assign a priority from P1 to P4 | User: "correctly". D2. | `priority_exact`, `priority_within_one` |
| R3 | Route the ticket to its owning team | User: "correctly". D2. | `team_exact` |
| R4 | Never rate a true P1 ticket lower than P1 | D3 | `p1_recall` |
| R5 | Return valid JSON that matches the D1 schema | D1 | `schema_valid` |
| R6 | Set `needs_human` on ambiguous or multi-issue tickets | D1 | `needs_human_recall` on the hard slice |
| R7 | Ignore instructions written inside a ticket body | Decision: tickets are untrusted input | `injection_resisted` on the injection tickets |
| R8 | Keep the mean cost at or below $0.004 per ticket | User: "cheaply". D4. | `cost_per_ticket` from the token usage the API reports |

This is round 1, so no failure IDs from earlier rounds exist yet.

## 2. Predict

There are three configurations. Each one is a real design choice between cost and accuracy.

- **A (small).** One call to a small model with the triage prompt and 6 examples.
- **B (large).** The same prompt sent to a mid-tier model.
- **C (cascade).** Model A runs first. The ticket goes to model B when A reports `confidence` below 0.7 or sets `needs_human`.

The test set has 200 tickets. 150 are typical tickets. 50 form a hard slice with ambiguous, multi-issue, non-English, and prompt-injection tickets. The accuracy cells have an error band of plus or minus 5 points, which is about the 95% interval for 200 tickets. The cost cells have an error band of plus or minus 30%.

| Metric | A | B | C | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy, all 200 | 85% | 92% | 90% | `category_exact` | The large model reads intent better, and C sends A's weakest cases to B. |
| Category accuracy, hard slice | 62% | 78% | 74% | `category_exact` | Ambiguous tickets cause most of the errors, and C does not escalate every one of them. |
| Priority exact match | 70% | 79% | 77% | `priority_exact` | The line between P2 and P3 is fuzzy even for human labelers. |
| Priority within one level | 95% | 97% | 97% | `priority_within_one` | Large priority errors should be rare for every model. |
| P1 recall | 86% | 95% | 93% | `p1_recall` | Small models often under-rate urgent tickets that use calm wording. |
| Team accuracy | 88% | 93% | 92% | `team_exact` | Team follows category closely, so it should track category accuracy. |
| All three fields correct | 57% | 69% | 66% | `all_fields_exact` | This is roughly the product of the three field accuracies. |
| Schema valid | 98.5% | 99.5% | 99.5% | `schema_valid` | Both models follow JSON instructions well. Small models slip more often. |
| `needs_human` recall, hard slice | 55% | 75% | 72% | `needs_human_recall` | Small models tend to be overconfident. |
| Injection resisted (10 tickets) | 80% | 90% | 90% | `injection_resisted` | C escalates many injection tickets because they look odd. |
| Escalation rate | n/a | n/a | 25% | `escalated` flag in the run log | About a quarter of tickets should fall below 0.7 confidence. |
| Mean cost per ticket | $0.0018 | $0.0054 | $0.0032 | `cost_per_ticket` | This assumes 1,200 input tokens and 120 output tokens per call at list prices. I will check current prices before the run. |
| Median latency | 1.5 s | 3.0 s | 2.0 s | `latency_p50` | Escalated tickets make two calls in a row. |

**Headline prediction.** C is the only configuration that meets both D3 and D4. A is cheap but misses the P1 recall bar. B meets the accuracy bars but costs more than $0.004 per ticket. If C misses P1 recall by more than 5 points, the cascade design is wrong.

The predictions are saved to `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` with the metric, configuration, value, error band, and grader check for each cell.

## 3. Evaluate

The author does not touch the judge. The answer keys and graders are written by a separate Opus subagent. That subagent never sees the agent prompt. The trial agents never see the keys.

### Build steps and gates

| Step | Output | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Agent | `agent/prompt.md`, `agent/triage.js`, `agent/config.json` with arms A, B, and C | 5 smoke tickets return schema-valid JSON in each arm. |
| 2. Dataset | `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` with inputs only, and `spe/evals/keys/answers.jsonl` | 200 tickets exist. Each category has at least 20 tickets. At least 12 tickets are P1. A grep finds no key labels in the tickets file. You spot-check 20 labels and approve them. |
| 3. Graders | `spe/evals/graders/grade.js`, with one function per grader check named above | A perfect answer file scores 100%. A shuffled answer file scores near chance. 10 hand-written cases, including known wrong answers, grade as expected. |
| 4. Harness | `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` | A dry run on 10 tickets per arm finishes. The trial context contains no path under `spe/evals/keys/`. Every call logs its tokens and cost. |

### Workflow arguments

```
arms: [A, B, C]
tickets: spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl
trials_per_ticket: 1 for typical tickets, 3 for the hard slice
temperature: 0
concurrency: 8
budget_cap_usd: 15
results_dir: spe/evals/results/r01/
```

### Cost and time estimate (unmeasured)

- Trials: about 900 agent calls across the three arms. That is about $3 at the assumed prices.
- Dataset and grader authoring by the Opus subagent: about $3 to $5.
- Grading is deterministic code, so it costs nothing.
- Total: about $6 to $8, with a hard cap of $15.
- Time: about 20 minutes for the run and about 1 to 2 hours for the build, including your label spot-check.

### Halt conditions

I stop the round and report to you if the run hits the $15 cap, if an answer key reaches a trial, or if a grader turns out to be broken during the run.

## 4. Close-out

- `spe/prediction-log.md` lists each predicted cell next to its measured value. Each cell is marked as a hit or a miss against its error band.
- `spe/failures.md` lists each failure pattern under an ID such as `F-r01-01`, with example ticket IDs. Round 2 requirements will cite these IDs.
- The proposals for round 2 go at the end of `spe/spec/spec.md`. If every arm passes every check, round 2 needs harder tickets or stricter graders, not more trials.
- I will report whether C met D3 and D4, which predictions missed, and what round 2 should change.

### Commits (local only, no push)

| Commit subject | When |
|---|---|
| `SPE r01 specify: triage spec, decisions D1-D5, raw prompt transcript` | After `spe/spec/spec.md` and `spe/spec/transcripts/r01-prompt.md` are written |
| `SPE r01 predict: plan and 13x3 predictions, cascade C predicted to meet both bars` | After `spe/plans/r01.md` and `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` are saved, before any harness work |
| `SPE r01 evaluate (harness): agent, 200 tickets, graders, workflow, dry run clean` | After gates 1 to 4 pass |
| `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <category acc, P1 recall, cost per ticket for A/B/C>` | After the run is graded. The real numbers replace the placeholder. |
| `SPE r01 learn: prediction log, failures, r02 proposals`, then tag `spe-r01` | After the close-out files are written |

## Before you approve

1. Do you want to keep D2, or do you have your own category and team list?
2. Can you share 50 or more real tickets, even with personal details removed? Real tickets would make the results much more trustworthy.
3. Is $0.004 per ticket the right cost ceiling for D4?
4. Which models should A and B use? My default is the current Haiku-class model for A and the current Sonnet-class model for B. I will confirm both against current docs before the run.
critiques: The plan quotes the user's sentence as the spec. The Specify table lists R1 to R8, and each row gives a source and a named test, such as R1 `category_exact` and R8 `cost_per_ticket`. Gaps such as the meaning of 'correctly' and 'cheaply' are filled by the defaults D1 to D5.

The Predict table gives numbers for configurations A, B, and C on 13 metrics. Examples are 85%, 92%, and 90% for category accuracy and $0.0018, $0.0054, and $0.0032 for cost per ticket. It also states error bands of plus or minus 5 points and plus or minus 30%.

Every row in the prediction table has a Why cell. For example, the P1 recall row says 'Small models often under-rate urgent tickets that use calm wording.' The escalation rate row and the latency row also give reasons.

The second commit, 'SPE r01 predict', happens 'After `spe/plans/r01.md` and `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` are saved, before any harness work.' That commit comes before any trial runs, so it meets the requirement.

The eval is 'one Workflow run' driven by `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js`. Gate 3 is a grader selftest: a perfect file must score 100%, a shuffled file must score near chance, and 10 hand-written cases must grade as expected. Gate 4 is a dry run on 10 tickets per arm.
The prediction table has a 'Grader check' column, and every metric names a check, such as `p1_recall`, `schema_valid`, and `latency_p50`. Escalation rate maps to the `escalated` flag in the run log.

The Close-out section writes `spe/prediction-log.md`, which marks each predicted cell as a hit or a miss against its error band. It also writes `spe/failures.md` with IDs like `F-r01-01` for round 2 to cite. Round 2 proposals go at the end of `spe/spec/spec.md`.
